entries.topic: The network before Herzl, 1836–1896: Kalischer's letter to Rothschild, the Alliance Israélite Universelle, Netter and Mikveh Israel, the Odessa Committee; added to the network map in Nov 2026

claims.text: Kalischer's 1836 letter to Amschel Mayer Rothschild, a Frankfurt banker and a stranger to him; his first attempt to act on his messianic theory; Rothschild as instrument of divine will.
EJ: Rothschild gave a noncommittal reply; Kalischer then approached Montefiore; correspondence lost (as recorded on the network map).

AIU launched May 1860 in Paris, first modern international Jewish organization; founder-members Carvallo, Cahen, Leven, Astruc, Manuel met at Netter's house; Damascus affair renewed urge for solidarity; Mortara case intensified drive for self-help; Crémieux president 1863–80; Netter opened Mikveh Israel 1870; after WWI opposed Zionism; 1945 pro-Zionist stand.

Netter a founder and treasurer of the Alliance; founded Mikveh Israel after the 1870 firman; in March 1882 publicly opposed immigration to Palestine; changed view later in 1882; died a month after arriving in August 1882.

Mortara: taken in Bologna 24 June 1858, aged six, by papal carabinieri on the inquisitor's orders after a servant said she had secretly baptised him; helped motivate the Alliance's founding in May 1860.

Odessa Committee: Society for the Support of Jewish Farmers and Artisans in Syria and Palestine, founded 1890 with Russian government permission; Pinsker, then Gruenberg from 1891, Ussishkin from 1906; supported Carmel winegrowers cooperative, Geulah land company, first donation toward a plot for the Hebrew University.
Odessa Committee counted over 4,000 members before the First Zionist Congress; funding mostly from charitable organizations in Europe and the US.
